title: Private by Default
concept: All items in XIOM are private unless explicitly marked `pub`
why: Private-by-default is a deliberate design choice that enforces encapsulation at the language level. It means you must consciously decide what to expose, rather than accidentally leaking implementation details. This principle has been validated by decades of software engineering: tight interfaces with hidden internals produce more maintainable, evolvable systems.
theory: In XIOM, every function, struct field, enum variant, constant, and type alias is private to its declaring module by default. This applies recursively: a public function in a private module is inaccessible; a public struct with private fields can be instantiated but not destructured. The compiler enforces these rules at the module boundary. Unlike some languages where 'private' means 'file-private', XIOM's privacy is module-scoped — child modules cannot access parent private items, but parent modules can access child `pub` items.
tips: Treat privacy as a design tool, not a restriction
Private helpers make refactoring safe — change them freely
Use `pub` as documentation: it signals 'this is the contract'
common_mistakes: Trying to access private fields from outside the module
Making everything public just to make code compile
Assuming child modules inherit parent visibility
